We need to propose a retrosynthesis route to target molecule with SMILES: O=S(NC1=CC(N2CCN(C(OC(C)(C)C)=O)CC2)=C3C(CCC4(CCC4)O3)=C1)(C5=C(F)C=CC=C5)=O

We need leaves commercially available, total price <=9999, steps <=6.

We have templates from search. The first template (reaction_id 20810) seems to disconnection of sulfonamide to sulfonyl chloride and an aniline? Actually template: product is sulfonamide attached to aryl, reactants: aryl sulfonyl chloride + aniline (with substituents). So we can disconnect the sulfonamide to sulfonyl chloride (aryl sulfonyl chloride) and the amine part (aryl amine). Our target has sulfonamide linking a sulfonyl group attached to two aryl groups: one is phenyl-F (para-fluoro phenyl) attached to sulfonyl, the other is a heteroaryl? Actually the sulfonyl attached to N which is attached to aromatic ring (a phenyl fused with bicyclic). The sulfonyl group is attached to N which is attached to aromatic ring (the N is part of an aniline). So we can break the S-N bond to get sulfonyl chloride (aryl sulfonyl chloride) and the aniline (aryl amine). The template 20810 seems to produce that.

Thus step 1: disconnection to aryl sulfonyl chloride (p-fluorophenyl sulfonyl chloride) and aniline containing the rest of molecule (the rest includes the N attached to aromatic system with N2CCN...). So we need to get those two fragments.

Fragment A: p-fluorophenyl sulfonyl chloride: SMILES: ClS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(F)cc1? Actually sulfonyl chloride: ClS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(F)cc1. That's commercially available likely.

Fragment B: the amine part: N-aryl with substituents: NC1=CC(N2CCN(C(OC(C)(C)C)=O)CC2)=C3C(CCC4(CCC4)O3)=C1. That's an aniline where the N is attached to the aromatic ring (the same N that was part of sulfonamide). So the fragment is an aniline with a side chain: N attached to aromatic ring, plus a substituent N2CCN(C(OC(C)(C)C)=O)CC2 (a tertiary amine with carbamate). Also the aromatic ring fused with a cyclohexanol? Actually there is a bicyclic system with a tertiary alcohol.

We need to further disconnect that fragment.

Potential disconnections: The carbamate (C(OC(C)(C)C)=O) attached to tertiary amine N. Could be formed via carbamoylation of the amine with t-butyl chloroformate (or t-butyl isocyanate). So we can disconnect the carbamate to give the tertiary amine (N2CCN(CC2) ) and t-butyl chloroformate (or t-butyl isocyanate). The template for carbamate formation likely exists.

Also the tertiary amine N2CCN... is a morpholine-like? Actually N2CCN(C(OC(C)(C)C)=O)CC2 is N,N-dialkylpiperazine? It's a piperazine with one nitrogen bearing the carbamate. So we could disconnect the piperazine ring? But maybe we can source the piperazine with appropriate substitution commercially.

The aromatic fused bicyclic system: C1=CC(... )=C3C(CCC4(CCC4)O3)=C1. This looks like a phenyl fused to a cyclohexanol (maybe a tetralone derivative). Could be derived from a phenol with a side chain.

We might consider a simpler route: Use commercially available building blocks: (1) p-fluorobenzenesulfonyl chloride (available). (2) 4-aminophenyl fused bicyclic with piperazine carbamate side chain. Might be too complex.

Alternative: Use template 214705 which disconnects sulfonamide into sulfonic acid and amine? Actually template 214705: retro_smarts: [O= S ... -[NH;D2] -[c] >> O-[S]... + NH2-aryl. That's similar.

Thus we need to get the amine fragment.

We can search for template to disconnect the piperazine carbamate: maybe a carbamate formation template.

Search for carbamate formation: functional_groups_formed ["carbamate"], broken maybe ["amines"]? Let's try.
